added.t: Changes in geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions could negatively affect Abbott's business, financial condition, and results of operations.

•additional challenges of doing business internationally, including differing local product preferences and product requirements, difficulty in establishing, staffing, and managing operations, and differing labor regulations;

•climate and public health-related events, including global climate change, extreme weather and natural disasters, public health crises such as widespread outbreaks of infectious diseases, and the cost and availability of insurance due to any of the foregoing …
•labor disputes, strikes, slow-downs, or other forms of labor or union activity, and pressure from third-party interest groups;

As a global healthcare company with sales outside of the U.S. making up approximately 61 percent of Abbott's net sales in 2025, Abbott's business is subject to geopolitical and macroeconomic risks that are beyond its control.
For example, the global economy has been impacted by geopolitical tensions focused on trade, which has increased uncertainty for global businesses such as Abbott.

removed.t: Abbott is subject to cost containment efforts that could cause a reduction in future revenues and operating income.

Abbott is subject to risks related to public health crises, such as widespread outbreaks of infectious diseases, which could have a material effect on Abbott's business, financial condition and results of operations.

For information on the impact that the COVID-19 pandemic had on Abbott's business, see the discussion in the "Financial Review" section in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, of this report.
The international nature of Abbott's business subjects it to additional business risks that may cause its revenue and profitability to decline.
•trade protection measures, including tariffs, import or export licensing requirements, other governmental restrictions such as trade sanctions, and changes to international trade agreements;
•potentially negative consequences from changes in or interpretations of tax laws;
•geopolitical and economic instability, including sovereign debt issues;
•restrictions on local currency conversion and/or cash extraction;
•price controls, limitations on participation in local enterprises, expropriation, nationalization, and other governmental action;

•potential penalties or other adverse consequences for violations of anti-corruption, anti-bribery, anti-competition, and other similar laws and regulations, including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the U.K. Bribery Act.
Events contemplated by these risks may, individually or in the aggregate, have a material adverse effect on Abbott's revenues and profitability.

As a global healthcare company, public health crises, such as the widespread outbreaks of infectious diseases, may negatively impact certain Abbott's operations.
Abbott's business is subject to risks associated with managing a global supply chain and doing business internationally.

Many of these factors may manifest individually or collectively, such as Russia's invasion of Ukraine which resulted in political instability, sanctions, economic and currency volatility, inflation and other operational and supply disruptions.
